Home.headline: Palworld Hub — Pal Data & Breeding Tools
Home.intro: A free hub for Palworld players. Browse Pal stats, find breeding combinations, and open guides for the Pals you care about.
Home.toolCalculatorBody: Pick two parents to see the child, or reverse look up every known way to breed a target Pal.
Home.toolPalsBody: Search the full Pal list, filter by element or work suitability, and open stats for every listed Pal.
Home.toolCombosBody: Browse parent + parent = child examples, unique recipes, and searchable combo guides for every breedable Pal.
Home.canDoTitle: What you can do on Palworld Hub
Home.canDo1Body: Use the <calculator>Palworld breeding calculator</calculator> for parent-to-child results and reverse parent lookups. When you already know the target, open its <combos>breeding combos</combos> page and search the full parent list.
Home.canDo2Body: Open the <pals>Palworld Pals</pals> list for combat stats, work suitability, partner skills, active skills, and drops — useful before you commit Cake and Breeding Farm time.
Home.canDo3Body: Send someone a <combos>Palworld breeding combos</combos> guide or Pal detail page when you already know the target. Every breedable Pal has a stable URL you can bookmark or drop in chat.
Home.howBody: Most sessions start one of two ways. If you already have two Pals in the Breeding Farm, open the calculator, pick both parents, and confirm the child before you spend Cake. If you want a specific Pal — Anubis for work, Jetragon for travel, or a base specialist — open that Pal’s breeding combos guide (or reverse lookup in the calculator) and pick a parent pair you can actually field.
Home.howTip: The child species depends on which two parents you pick — not on which one is male or female. Some special pairs always make a fixed unique child.
Home.combosBody: Prefer reading a full list instead of tapping through the calculator? The breeding combos database shows real parent + parent = child examples, unique recipes, and a searchable guide for every breedable Pal — including what that Pal produces when used as a parent.
Home.dataBody: Palworld Hub tracks the live game data we import for breeding recipes, unique pairs, and Pal details. When Pocketpair ships balance or content changes, we refresh the tables so the calculator and guides stay useful for planning farms and base teams. Always double-check critical results in your own game after a major patch.
Home.whoBody: Whether you are optimizing a base crew, hunting a legendary mount, or helping a friend hatch their first rare Pal, the goal is the same: fewer wasted Cakes and clearer next steps. Palworld Hub is free, unofficial, and focused on the lookups players actually need — stats, combos, and reverse breeding — without account walls.
Home.popularBreedingDescription: Quick links to dedicated breeding guides — open the calculator when you need a full reverse lookup.
Home.popularPalsDescription: Jump into detail pages for frequently searched Pals, or browse the full database.

Calculator.title: Palworld Breeding Calculator
Calculator.description: Wondering what two Pals will hatch? Pick the parents and see the child right away — or name the Pal you want and find parent pairs that can produce it. No guessing, no wasted Cake.
Calculator.summary: {breedable} breedable Pals · {unique} unique recipes · data for {version}
Calculator.genderBody: Katress × Wixen is a special case in Palworld: which parent is female changes the child. Choose the female parent to match your Breeding Farm.
Calculator.noResult: No breeding result for this pair.
Calculator.reverseTitle: Find how to breed a target Pal
Calculator.reverseHint: Select a target Pal to see breeding combinations.
Calculator.noCombinations: No known combinations for this Pal yet.
Calculator.howToTitle: How to use this breeding calculator
Calculator.howToForwardBody: Got two Pals ready for the Breeding Farm? Select them as Parent 1 and Parent 2. The child shows up immediately — including special unique recipes when those parents match one. From there you can check the child’s stats or switch modes to hunt for more parent pairs.
Calculator.howToReverseBody: Already know what you want — Anubis for the base, Jetragon for travel, Frostallion, or something else? Switch to Target → Parents, pick that Pal, and scan the parent pairs you can actually farm toward instead of testing random couples.
Calculator.worksP1: In-game, the same two parents always hatch the same child species. You still need one male, one female, and Cake at the Breeding Farm — but which one is male or female does not change the child species, and swapping parent order does not either.
Calculator.worksP2: For most pairs, the game blends the two parents and lands on a nearby breedable Pal. That is why lots of different couples still hatch the same common eggs — especially in the middle of the Paldex.
Calculator.worksP3: A smaller set of pairs are special recipes. Those fixed combinations always make a specific child (Lux / Cryst lines and similar uniques) and override the normal result when they apply.
Calculator.worksP4: This calculator follows the same order as the game: unique recipes first, then normal breeding. Plan your farm before you spend Cake. After a big patch, double-check anything important in your own world.
Calculator.popularDescription: Jump to a full combo list for that Pal, or load it here as the target for a quick reverse lookup.
Calculator.faq1Q: What can this breeding calculator do?
Calculator.faq1A: Two jobs: tell you what child two parents will produce, or list parent pairs that can hatch a Pal you already want. Use it before you put Cake in the Breeding Farm.
Calculator.faq2Q: How do I find ways to breed a specific Pal?
Calculator.faq2A: Switch to Target → Parents, choose the Pal you want, and browse the parent pairs. Want a longer searchable list? Open that Pal’s full combo guide from the links under the results.
Calculator.faq3Q: Does gender or parent order change the child?
Calculator.faq3A: Not the species. You still need one male and one female (plus Cake) for the Breeding Farm to run, but which parent is which gender does not change the egg. Parent order does not matter either — A with B is the same as B with A.
Calculator.faq4Q: Why do so many pairs hatch the same common Pal?
Calculator.faq4A: That is just how normal breeding works in Palworld — a lot of mid-tier couples land on nearby common eggs. If you want something rarer, use Target → Parents for that Pal, or look for a unique recipe pair.
Calculator.faq5Q: Is the calculator up to date?
Calculator.faq5A: It uses our current game data for {version}, including unique recipes and normal breeding results. Patches can change things — if a hatch surprises you after an update, tell us and we will refresh the tables.
Calculator.exploreBody: Browse Palworld Pals for stats and work suitability, or open the breeding combos database when you want shareable parent-pair guides.
Calculator.datasetDescription: Palworld breeding combination data used by the Palworld breeding calculator, including unique recipes and formula-based parent-to-child results.

Pals.guideTitle: How to use this Palworld Pals list
Pals.guideBody: Search by name if you already know who you want. Looking for a Kindling or Mining worker? Filter by work suitability. Building an elemental team? Filter by element. Open any Pal for stats, partner skill, drops, and breeding links.
Pals.faq1Q: How many Pals are in this list?
Pals.faq1A: Right now we list {total} Palworld Pals for {version}. Other sites may show a different number if they count subspecies, event entries, or raid-only Pals differently — so treat every Paldex total as “for this list,” not a universal law.
Pals.faq2Q: How do I find a good Pal for my base?
Pals.faq2A: Use the work suitability filter above (Kindling, Watering, Mining, Handiwork, Transporting, and the rest). Higher work levels usually mean better base performance for that job. Open a few candidates and compare their partner skills and combat stats before you commit catch or breeding time.
Pals.faq3A: Nocturnal Pals stay productive at night when many daytime workers sleep. If your base stalls after dark, filter or scan for nocturnal Pals and keep at least a couple on the crew for power, cooling, or transport.
Pals.faq4A: No. This list marks {breedable} as breedable. Some raid bosses and special Pals cannot produce eggs — you have to earn those in-game instead. If a Pal is breedable, its page links to combo guides and the breeding calculator.
Pals.faq5Q: I know the Pal I want — how do I get it?
Pals.faq5A: Search the name (or Paldex number) in the box above, open its page, then use the breeding section or jump to that Pal’s combo guide / the breeding calculator to find parent pairs. Catching in the wild still works when the egg route is painful.
Pals.faq6Q: What should I look at on a Pal’s detail page?
Pals.faq6A: For base building: work suitability and partner skill. For fights and exploration: elements, HP / attack / defense, and movement or mount speeds. Drops matter if you farm materials. Breeding links are there when you decide to hatch one instead of catching it.

BreedingHub.title: Palworld Breeding Combos
BreedingHub.description: Find Palworld breeding combos fast: see real parent + parent = child examples below, browse unique recipes, then open a Pal guide for every pair that produces it — or what it breeds as a parent.
BreedingHub.featuredDescription: Special fixed recipes from the current game data. Each card is a real parent + parent = child combo — click the child to open its full guide.
BreedingHub.popularDescription: High-demand Pals with example parent pairs. Open a guide for the full searchable combo list.
BreedingHub.allDescription: Every breedable Pal has a dedicated breeding combos page: parents that produce it, and outcomes when it is used as a parent.
BreedingHub.howTitle: How to use these breeding combos
BreedingHub.howBody: A breeding combo is simply “these two parents hatch this child.” Most pairs follow normal breeding rules; a smaller set of unique recipes always make a fixed child. Skim the examples below, search a Pal you want, then open its guide for the full parent list — or what it produces when used as a parent.
BreedingHub.howTipBody: You still need one male, one female, and Cake at the Breeding Farm. For almost every pair, which parent is which gender does not change the child species — only the two species you pick matter. On a Pal’s guide, use Breed to farm that Pal, or As parent to see partner outcomes.
BreedingHub.faq1A: It’s a parent pair that hatches a specific child Pal. Same two parents → same child species. This page shows real examples and links to a full guide for every breedable Pal so you can plan before you burn Cake.
BreedingHub.faq2Q: How do I find every way to breed a Pal I want?
BreedingHub.faq2A: Search that Pal in “Browse breeding guides,” open its page, and stay on the Breed tab. You’ll get parent pairs that produce it. Popular targets above also jump straight into those guides.
BreedingHub.faq3Q: What does “as parent” mean on a Pal’s guide?
BreedingHub.faq3A: That’s the reverse view: pick the Pal you already own and see what child you get with each partner. Useful when you’re deciding who to put in the farm next, not just how to hatch one specific egg.
BreedingHub.faq4Q: Do I need Cake? Does gender change the child?
BreedingHub.faq4A: Yes to Cake — no Cake, no egg. You also need one male and one female assigned to the Breeding Farm. For almost all combos, swapping which species is male or female does not change the child. A few special pairs are the exception; if a guide mentions one, follow that pairing.
BreedingHub.faq5Q: What are the “unique recipes” at the top?
BreedingHub.faq5A: Fixed special pairs that always make the same child and override normal breeding. They’re the ones people usually mean by Lux / Cryst-style lines and similar uniques. Click the child on a card to see the full guide.
BreedingHub.faq6Q: Should I use this page or the breeding calculator?
BreedingHub.faq6A: Use this page when you want to browse, compare, or bookmark a Pal’s full combo list. Use the calculator when you already have two parents in mind — or a target Pal — and want an instant answer without digging through the directory.
BreedingHub.empty: No breeding guides matched your search.

About.title: About {siteName}
About.intro: Hey — thanks for stopping by. {siteName} is a small fan project I built because I kept tabbing between spreadsheets, Discord pins, and half-remembered breeding pairs mid-session. I’m a developer, but I’m also just another Palworld player who wanted a cleaner place to check stats and plan hatches.
About.s1Body: I’ve lost count of how many Cakes I’ve burned on a “probably right” parent pair. Palworld’s breeding rules are elegant once you see them, and painful when you don’t. I wanted something fast: pick two parents, see the child; or name the Pal I actually want and see real combos I can farm toward. Same for the Pal list — work suitability and partner skills matter at the base as much as shiny combat numbers.
About.s2Body: You’ll find a Pal database (stats, work, skills, drops), a breeding calculator (parents → child and reverse lookup), and breeding combo guides you can bookmark or send to a friend. I keep the tools practical on purpose — less fluff, more “what do I put in the Breeding Farm next.”
About.s3Body: The numbers and recipes come from game-derived tables I import and refresh when the live game changes. I’m careful, but I’m not Pocketpair — patches happen, edge cases slip through, and your save is the final judge. If something looks wrong, tell me. Fixing a bad combo feels better than arguing with a wiki tab at 2 a.m.
About.s4Body: {siteName} is unofficial. I’m not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Pocketpair or any Palworld rights holder. Palworld and related names, characters, and assets belong to their owners. This is a fan tool made with respect for the game — and with the hope it saves you a few wasted Cakes.
About.s5Body: Spot a wrong result, have a feature idea, or just want to talk breeding routes?
